title: Musk's Speech Revealed: Launching Deep Integration After Spending 6 Billion to Acquire Cursor

content_html:
Recently, SpaceX completed a major acquisition of AI programming tool company Cursor for as much as 6 billion dollars. After the transaction, Elon Musk addressed the more than a thousand employees of Cursor in an internal all-hands meeting, publicly acknowledging for the first time that SpaceX's artificial intelligence department is currently behind strong competitors like Anthropic in the fierce industry competition.

In this speech, Musk not only faced the reality of technological lag but also emphasized that artificial intelligence technology will eventually reach a stage where it is beyond human control, and he urged all employees to spare no effort to help him seize key technologies ahead of others. He also clearly stated that he would continue to mass-purchase computing power in the future.

Since the official signing of the technology sharing and computing power cooperation agreement in April this year, SpaceX's influence has continued to spread within Cursor. In terms of business and resources, Cursor has obtained sufficient recruitment budget to accelerate team expansion and is fully advancing the Origin project, which is comparable to GitHub, as well as related beta versions.

However, during this grand acquisition and integration process, there have been significant upheavals within Cursor. Although the management had previously claimed that the transaction would have limited impact on daily operations, many people left when it was implemented, including several senior leaders and core members of the Graphite team. At the same time, the company also adjusted its equity vesting policy, demoted some senior executives, and made changes to the overall compensation plan. With the completion of the acquisition, the executive team of Cursor has officially joined SpaceX AI in key positions, and in-depth team integration work between the two companies is now fully underway.

Looking back at its development history, Cursor has experienced rapid expansion in recent years. This code editor tool provider, originally founded by a team from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), has continuously expanded its business boundaries due to increasingly intense industry competition. Previously, due to negative gross profit margins that hindered fundraising, the company ultimately chose to partner with SpaceX to obtain computing power support and jointly invest in the development of the new Grok model and related AI agents.
